tools.name: Glob
tools.description:
Find files by glob pattern, sorted by modification time (most recent first).

Powered by ripgrep. Respects `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` by default — set `include_ignored` to also match ignored files (e.g. build outputs, `node_modules`). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) are always filtered out. Matches are files only — directories themselves are never listed; to find a directory, glob for a file inside it (e.g. `**/fixtures/**`).

Good patterns:
- `*.ts` — all files matching an extension, at any depth below the search root (a bare pattern without `/` matches recursively)
- `src/*.ts` — files directly inside `src/` (one level, not recursive)
- `src/**/*.ts` — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor and extension
- `**/*.py` — recursive walk from the search root for an extension
- `*.{ts,tsx}` — brace expansion is supported
- `{src,test}/**/*.ts` — cartesian brace expansion is supported too

Results are capped at the first 100 matching paths. If a search would return more, a truncation marker is appended. Refine the pattern (extension, subdirectory) when 100 is not enough, or call again with a narrower anchor.

Large-directory caveat — avoid recursing into dependency / build output even with an anchor, especially when `include_ignored` is set:
- `node_modules/**/*.js`, `.venv/**/*.py`, `__pycache__/**`, `target/**` can produce thousands of results that truncate at the match cap and waste context. Prefer specific subpaths like `node_modules/react/src/**/*.js`.

include_ignored.description: Also match files excluded by ignore files such as `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.rgignore` (for example `node_modules` or build outputs). Sensitive files (such as `.env`) remain filtered out for safety. VCS metadata directories (`.git` and similar) are always skipped, even when this is true. Defaults to false.

include_dirs.description: Deprecated and ignored. Results are always files-only — directories are never listed. Accepted only so older calls that still pass this flag are not rejected by parameter validation.

# test18 — Query/Fragment Behavior Report (black-box)

## Interface

- Usage: `test18_executable <url>` — only `argv[1]` is parsed, extra args ignored.
- No args → no output, exit code **1**. Any single argument (even `""`, garbage) → exit code **0**.
- Output: 18 newline-separated fields on stdout:

| # | Field | # | Field |
|---|-------|---|-------|
| 1 | scheme (lowercased) | 10 | flag: host non-empty |
| 2 | authority (recomposed: `[userinfo@]host[:port]`) | 11 | flag: userinfo non-empty |
| 3 | userinfo | 12 | flag: host non-empty (identical to flag 10 in all 35+ probes) |
| 4 | host | 13 | flag: valid port present |
| 5 | port (`-1` if absent/invalid) | 14 | flag: path non-empty |
| 6 | path | 15 | flag: query non-empty |
| 7 | query (no `?`) | 16 | flag: fragment non-empty |
| 8 | fragment (no `#`) | 17 | reconstructed URL |
| 9 | flag: scheme non-empty | 18 | "valid" = host OR path non-empty |

Baseline `http://example.com/path?query=1#frag` → `http|example.com||example.com|-1|/path|query=1|frag|1|1|0|1|0|1|1|1|http://example.com/path?query=1#frag|1`, exit 0.

## Parse order (inferred)

1. Split at **first `#`** → fragment = rest (may contain `?`, `#`). Then split remainder at **first `?`** → query = rest (may contain `?`). Only then scheme/`://`/authority/path on what remains.
2. Consequences:
   - `?a?b` → query `a?b`; `??` → query `?` (non-empty, flag set).
   - `#a#b` → fragment `a#b`; `##` → fragment `#`; `?q#f#` → fragment `f#`.
   - `#frag?query` → query empty, fragment `frag?query` (`?` after `#` belongs to fragment).
   - `?` truncates the authority: `http://user?x@host/path?q#f` → host `user`, path empty, query `x@host/path?q`.
   - `#` truncates everything: `http://exa#mple.com/path?x` → host `exa`, path/query empty, fragment `mple.com/path?x`.

## Empty query/fragment — surprising

- `?`, `#`, `?#`, trailing `#` produce **empty** component → flag 0, and reconstruction **drops the delimiter**:
  - `http://example.com/path?` → recon `http://example.com/path`
  - `http://example.com/path?#f` → query empty; recon `http://example.com/path#f` (dangling `?` removed)
  - `http://example.com/path?q#` → recon `http://example.com/path?q`
- So reconstruction is **not** identity whenever an empty query/fragment marker was present; otherwise it is exact.

## Percent-encoding / delimiters / case

- **No decoding, no validation, no re-encoding.** `%41`, `%20`, `%23`, `%3F`, even malformed `%zz`, `%2`, `%gg` pass through verbatim in every component; `%3F`/`%23` in query do **not** split. Recon preserves them exactly.
- `+` kept literally (no space conversion): `?a+b=c+d` → `a+b=c+d`.
- All delimiters inside query preserved: `& = ; , : /` (`?a=b;c=d,e=f:g/h` untouched). `;param` stays in path.
- Spaces are ordinary chars — no trimming: `"  http://…/p?q#f  "` → scheme `"  http"`, fragment `"f  "`.
- Scheme is **lowercased** (`HTTP`→`http`, `HtTp`→`http`); host/path/query/fragment case preserved (`EXAMPLE.COM`, `Q=1`, `F`).
- Backslash is ordinary: `http://example.com\path?q#f` → host `example.com\path`, path empty.

## Scheme/authority quirks (context for flags)

- Scheme recognized **only via `://`**: `mailto:user@example.com?subject=x#f` → scheme empty, path `mailto:user@example.com`. `h2+1.0://…` works and is lowercased.
- No scheme → entire pre-`?` text is the path: `example.com/path?q#f` → host empty, path `example.com/path`.
- `://host/p?q#f` (empty scheme) → host `host`, path `/p` parsed, **but** reconstruction is `/p?q#f` — authority silently dropped when scheme is empty.
- userinfo split at **first `@`**: `http://a@b@c/` → userinfo `a`, host `b@c`.
- Port parsed like `strtol` + range check 0–65535, then re-emitted numerically: `:08080`→`8080`, `:+80`→`80`, `:80x`→`80`; `:abc`, `:`, `:-1`, `:65536`, `:99999999999999` → port `-1` and **port dropped from authority and reconstruction** (`http://example.com:abc/p` → recon `http://example.com/p`).

## Field-18 "valid" flag

1 iff host or path non-empty. `http://?query` → 0; `?q=1#f`, `#f`, `?q`, `""`, `http://` → 0; `/p?q#f`, `example.com/p`, `http:///path` → 1. Query/fragment alone never make it valid. Exit code is 0 regardless.
